title: Iterative Retrieval for Multi-Hop Question Answering
contextual_summary: Directly relevant. Compares iterative retrieval against a 128k long-context baseline on two multi-hop benchmarks. Controls for token budget, not retrieval recall, so it does not settle our question, but it is the closest existing design. Ablation suggests the gain narrows as context grows. No variance over seeds reported.
claim: Iterative retrieval beats a 128k long-context baseline by 6.2 EM on a 2-hop benchmark at matched token budget; the gap narrows above 64k context.

title: Long-Context Models Are Strong Multi-Hop Reasoners
contextual_summary: The counter-position: keyword search never returned it because it uses different vocabulary, and the mainstream papers do not cite it. It argues that long-context models match retrieval pipelines once context is sufficient — the opposite direction to alpha2025iterative on an overlapping benchmark. Neither controls retrieval recall, so the disagreement is unresolved rather than contradictory.
claim: A 128k long-context model matches an iterative retrieval pipeline within 1.1 EM on 2-hop QA at equal token budget.

title: Scaling Multi-Hop Depth
contextual_summary: Extends evaluation to 3+ hops but only for iterative methods; no long-context arm. It fills the 3+-hop row for one method and leaves the comparison open. Read to method level only — results not yet checked against tables.
claim: The authors report that iterative retrieval degrades gracefully to 4 hops; the accuracy figures behind that report have not been read from the tables.

title: Retrieval Augmentation Revisited
contextual_summary: Single-hop only. Same keywords, different problem.

title: Toward Recall-Controlled Comparison
contextual_summary: Workshop abstract, two pages. Proposes matching retrieval recall across arms — exactly our gap — but reports no results and the full paper is not available. It remains unresolved.
